verdict: Avoid new tea plantation exposure in Agartala for now; the new auction centre is a real positive but too new to underwrite, and Tripura's local demand signal is weak — lend only to small growers with auction-linked receivables and tight monthly structure.
title: Agartala Tea Plantations: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A tea garden turns leaf into made tea and cash, and the cash sits far from the bush.** Green leaf is plucked, withered, rolled, fermented, dried and sorted within hours; the output is bulk made tea sold in lots, not branded packets. Cost is dominated by plucking labour and firewood/power for the factory; pricing power is near zero for a bulk seller, so realisation is set by the auction. **So when a proposal lands, check the factory's own cost per kg of made tea and the share of leaf bought from small growers versus own estate; if the borrower cannot state both, ask for the previous season's cost sheet.**

## What has changed now
**Tripura's first tea auction centre opened at PN Complex in Agartala, which the CM says will help producers secure better prices and reduce transportation costs [1][2][3].** That is genuinely the biggest structural change for a Tripura garden in years — it shortens the chain to the buyer and puts a local price discovery point on the borrower's doorstep. But it is days old, so there is no track record of realisations through it; collect from customer the first three months of auction sale prices and the commission charged. **Separately, Tripura's electricity demand fell 1.7% Apr-to-date against India's +9.5% [D] — a local activity signal that argues against funding capacity expansion right now.**

## Where the growth is, and who to avoid
**Pursue small tea growers and bought-leaf factories that will now sell through the Agartala centre, because their receivable is a documented auction sale rather than a distant broker's word.** Peer evidence says the money in tea is thin: Crisil saw plantation revenue down 8% in FY24 with operating margin at 5% [7], and Rossell's tea business earns 5-10% EBITDA against 20-30% in its aerospace arm [4]. ## How to grow safely
**Structure against the auction receivable, not the land.** Sanction a cash credit sized to one auction cycle, with the auction centre's sale statement as the drawing base, and take the sale proceeds through an escrow at our branch. **Take every month: auction sale statements, leaf purchase and plucking labour cost, power bill, and stock of made tea with godown verification.** Covenant a minimum realisation per kg and a cap on bought-leaf dependence. If the borrower resists escrow, ask why the sale cannot be routed through us. ## Early warning signs
**Watch for sale statements that stop arriving or shift to a private buyer, power bills falling faster than plucking volumes, and wage arrears to plucking gangs.** Any of these means the auction benefit is not reaching the borrower's cash cycle.
watch: No statement for one cycle -> stop drawing power and inspect godown
Realisation per kg vs sanctioned base (monthly)
Falls below covenant for two months -> cut limit and seek fresh cost sheet
Bill falls with volumes flat -> ask for plucking and stock records
Arrears reported -> freeze new disbursal and review
Sale proceeds bypass escrow -> treat as diversion, recall
